articles.title: Fifty Authorizations Is Not an Attack: 30 Blocks of EIP-7702 Data
articles.excerpt: On 2026-10-30 a major exchange's hot wallets were drained. Public reporting says the attackers never saw a private key — they got the signing infrastructure to sign 50 EIP-7702 authorizations in one t…
articles.body: On 2026-10-30 a major exchange's hot wallets were drained. Public reporting says the attackers never saw a private key — they got the signing infrastructure to sign 50 EIP-7702 authorizations in one transaction. I wrote a decoder to look for that shape on-chain. I found it in the first 30 blocks. It was a product, not an attack. The claim I wanted to test Reports described the pattern as: one transaction, dozens of authorization_list entries, nonce values in sequence, all landing in a single block. If that shape is the signature of the attack, then a simple rule — more than N authorizations in one transaction = suspicious — should find it. So I built the smallest tool that could check: RLP decoding, keccak256, secp256k1 recovery, no web3 dependency.
articles.author: rytjy

articles.title: Replacing long-lived AWS keys: testing Vault's options with an AI co-worker
articles.excerpt: What we are testing before choosing how Vault issues AWS credentials, what assumed_role revealed, and where AI-generated tests still needed an engineer. Replacing long-lived AWS keys sounds straightfo…
articles.body: What we are testing before choosing how Vault issues AWS credentials, what assumed_role revealed, and where AI-generated tests still needed an engineer. Replacing long-lived AWS keys sounds straightforward: issue credentials that expire, and stop leaving permanent access in build systems, laptops and old scripts. We already use HashiCorp Vault to manage secrets. It can issue AWS credentials in four different ways. Before choosing one for wider use, we wanted to understand how each behaves when access is granted, restricted or revoked. I used an AI-assisted workflow to help with the evaluation. Agents prepared test plans, reviewed one another's work, wrote scripts and turned execution logs into reports. I reviewed the scripts, ran them in a sandbox and checked the conclusions.

articles.title: Hotel POS Software Development: How to Split One Guest Bill Across Room, Card and Corporate Accounts
articles.excerpt: A hotel guest may order breakfast at the restaurant, enjoy drinks at the bar, request room service, and charge everything to the same room. At checkout, however, the guest might want accommodation and…
articles.body: A hotel guest may order breakfast at the restaurant, enjoy drinks at the bar, request room service, and charge everything to the same room. At checkout, however, the guest might want accommodation and breakfast billed to a corporate account, minibar purchases paid by card, and personal dining expenses settled separately. This is where hotel POS software development becomes more complex than ordinary retail billing. The system must split charges accurately, communicate with the hotel property management system (PMS), and ensure that every payment and room posting remains traceable. A well-designed hotel point-of-sale system should not treat a guest bill as a single payment record.

articles.title: Why I Built 150+ In-Browser Privacy Tools (0 Cloud Uploads)
articles.excerpt: Every single working day, millions of people drag sensitive documents into online converters: Signed legal agreements and employment contracts Tax returns and bank account statements Medical patient r…
articles.body: Every single working day, millions of people drag sensitive documents into online converters: Signed legal agreements and employment contracts Tax returns and bank account statements Medical patient reports and confidential scans Production JSON responses containing customer PII and private API keys Most people assume these popular converter sites simply process the file and delete it. But when you look at the network tab of standard online utilities, you see multi-megabyte POST requests transmitting your private data to unknown cloud servers across the globe. Even if a service promises to delete files after one hour, server-side data leaks, misconfigured Amazon S3 buckets, and third-party tracking remain constant threats.

articles.body: A long keyword spreadsheet is not a site architecture. The useful deliverable is a map that tells your team which user need each page serves, how people reach it, and what should happen next. This guide uses an imaginary coffee store. The queries and paths are examples, not measured search volumes or claims about a real search results page. Start with the business boundary List the products, services, audiences and locations the site actually serves. A coffee retailer may have a bean catalogue, brewing equipment and delivery information. If it does not repair machines, a repair-service landing page would promise something the business cannot deliver. For an existing site, inventory current URLs before proposing new ones.

articles.title: Agent.reviews: How AI Agents Write Product Reviews and What It Reveals About Tool Feedback Loops
articles.excerpt: Armature (YC P26) measured 50,000+ agent sessions and found agents repeatedly hit the same tool limitations. The feedback loop that would fix these issues doesn't exist. Human users file GitHub issues…
articles.body: Armature (YC P26) measured 50,000+ agent sessions and found agents repeatedly hit the same tool limitations. The feedback loop that would fix these issues doesn't exist. Human users file GitHub issues or support tickets. Agents just fail silently, retry with exponential backoff, or hallucinate workarounds. Agent.reviews is Armature's response: a platform where agents write reviews based on actual usage patterns. The site indexes tools (FastAPI, Supabase, Auth0, Modal, uv, OpenAI API) and publishes agent-generated reviews with numeric ratings. Each review describes what the agent tried, what worked, and what broke. The interesting part is not the review content.

articles.title: Think Halloween is scary? This scorched alien world is a real-life cosmic horror story
articles.excerpt: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the JWST, if it wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface.
articles.body: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). That is, if this extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface. The exoplanet in question is the rocky lava planet TOI-561 b, located around 280 light-years away, which was discovered by NASA's exoplanet-hunting spacecraft TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) in 2020. The planet is located so close to its star, TOI-561, that not only does it complete an orbit every 11 hours, but its surface temperatures reach in excess of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,800 degrees Celsius). That is so hot that astronomers once believed that TOI-561 b couldn't possibly possess an atmosphere.

articles.body: Less than a week after the fates took Walter Koenig from our galaxy, another " Star Trek " legend has left us: Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. According to his spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak, the beloved Shakespearean actor passed away on Wednesday (Oct. 28) at his Los Angeles home after a short struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all," Bush Novak shared.
